title: Pattern Lab: Documentation for components, tokens, and deprecation paths
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a focused "pattern lab" section in the design docs that consolidates usage guidelines, live examples, do/don't patterns, migration notes, and component API snippets for tokens, buttons, tables, and charts. The goal is to make it easy for engineers and product teams to adopt the new tokens and component APIs with minimal friction and clear rollback/deprecation guidance.
background: Over the last two quarters we've shipped token renames and a refactor of the Button and Table components. We received feedback that adoption is slow because the docs are fragmented: token docs live in tokens.md, component examples are in Storybook, and migration notes are scattered in PRs/drive. This ticket centralizes guidance, provides concrete code examples, and defines a deprecation path for legacy props/variables.
goals: Ship a Pattern Lab section on docs.redwood.ai with canonical usage cards for tokens, buttons, tables, and charts.
Include explicit do/don't patterns and visual regressions for each example.
Provide a step-by-step migration guide from legacy token names and props to the current design-system API.
Publish mapping tables (old -> new) and an automated codemod link + sample outputs.
Ensure Storybook examples link to docs and vice versa; add stability notes and suggested fallbacks.
Add a deprecation timeline and maintainers/owners for follow-up questions.
acceptance_criteria: Pattern Lab page is available under /pattern-lab with individual subsections for tokens, buttons, tables, charts.
Each component subsection contains: short summary, when-to-use, do/don't, API surface with TypeScript code snippets, and 3-4 runnable examples (small/medium/complex).
Migration notes include token mapping CSV, recommended codemod (link), and manual steps for edge cases.
QA: Visual inspection screenshots added for before/after when migrating tokens for Buttons and Tables.
Docs cross-linking: Storybook example pages include a banner linking to the Pattern Lab; docs include links to the GitHub PR and confluence design spec.
Design review signed off by design leads and handoff noted in the PR description.

decisions: Pattern Lab will live in docs.redwood.ai under /pattern-lab instead of Storybook to reduce duplication and allow richer prose.
Examples should prioritize minimal reproducible examples (React + TS) with a link to raw code and a live sandbox. Full app examples will live in a separate 'reference apps' section.
We will provide both CSS variable examples (for non-React consumers) and React/TSX examples to accommodate multiple stacks.
Deprecation window for legacy token names set to 12 weeks from release; codemod will handle 80% conversions, manual steps documented for the rest.
tradeoffs: Keeping Pattern Lab in docs (vs Storybook) loses Storybook's isolated environment but gains searchable prose and richer migration content.
Providing both CSS and React examples increases maintenance cost but lowers adoption friction for non-React teams.
A 12-week deprecation window accelerates progress but requires better developer comms and automated tooling to avoid breakage.
notes: Reference GitHub PR for token rename: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pull/512
migration_steps: 1) Audit: Run the provided token-audit script across repos to identify occurrences of legacy tokens.
2) Automated: Run the codemod from the codemod repo and review changes. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/codemods/pull/1
3) Manual fixes: Review edge cases where tokens were composed at runtime; follow the manual checklist in the migration guide.
4) QA: Add visual snapshot tests for updated components (Buttons/Tables) and compare to baseline screenshots from before migration.
5) Rollout: Merge changes behind feature flags if high-risk; otherwise coordinate a line-change release with a short maintenance window.
component_guidelines: Tokens: Prefer semantic tokens (e.g., --rwd-color-accent) over raw hex values. Document token intent and recommended fallbacks.
Buttons: Use Button.Variant prop for intent (primary/secondary/ghost). Avoid inline style overrides—use variants & token overrides.
Tables: Encourage use of Table.Paginated for large datasets; include guidance on column density and responsive behavior.
Charts: Provide pattern examples for small multiples vs single large chart and guidance on color token usage for accessibility.
Do/Don'ts: Each card shows a short snippet labeled DO (good) and DON'T (anti-pattern) with reasoning.
api_snippets:
// Table example (paginated)
<Table.Paginated columns={cols} data={rows} pageSize={25} onFetch={fetchPage} />

// Chart example (using rwd tokens for colors)
<BarChart data={series} colors={["var(--rwd-color-accent)", "var(--rwd-color-muted)"]} />
visual_examples: Small button variations (primary/secondary/disabled) with before/after token mapping screenshots attached in PR.
Table density examples (compact/comfortable/expanded) showing padding/token differences.
Chart color palette permutations demonstrating accessible contrast -- referenced in docs with WCAG notes.
review_feedback: Eli: Please add a short troubleshooting section for token collisions when a repo defines local overrides.
Priya: Request 2 extra QA passes for the codemod-run repos; add a checklist for rollbacks.
Sam: Recommend adding a short 'how we tested this' subsection showing snapshot comparisons and performance notes for charts.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Build page templates, extract snippets, create token mapping CSV.
Week 2: Hook up live sandboxes, ship initial docs, announce to early adopters, gather feedback.
Week 3: Run codemod across a subset of repos, ship fixes, and prepare deprecation emails.
Week 4: Widen rollout and close loop on feedback; update docs with common edge-case workarounds.
risks: Codemod false positives/negatives causing regressions — mitigated with review and feature flags.
Consumers using inline tokens creating migration complexity — mitigated with clear manual steps and examples.
Lack of visibility: if docs aren't discoverable, adoption will lag — mitigate with cross-links and in-product banners.
announcements: Post draft on #design-system announcing Pattern Lab launch and link to feedback form: https://forms.redwood.ai/pattern-lab-feedback
Email to internal eng teams with migration checklist and codemod usage instructions scheduled for Week 3.
